We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings; on the second phenyl, there is a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (cinnamoyl amide) attached to an aniline (anilide). So three steps: likely disconnections:

1. Disconnection of amide bond: break C(=O)N between the α,β-unsaturated acid and the aniline (c3ccccc3N). So retrosynthesis: amide formation from carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline. So precursor: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (cinnamic acid derivative) attached to phenyl sulfonamide core.

2. Disconnection of the α,β-unsaturated acid formation via Doebner modification: from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl sulfonamide bearing aldehyde) and malonic acid to give the α,β-unsaturated acid. So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide with aldehyde at para position relative to sulfonamide? Actually the target has /C=C/ attached to phenyl ring at position para to sulfonamide? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl. So the phenyl ring (c2) has the side chain at para position relative to sulfonamide? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonamide attaches at position 1 of that phenyl, and the side chain at position 4 (para). So we can imagine an aldehyde at that position for Doebner.

Thus precursor: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(=O)?? Actually aldehyde is -CHO). So we need phenyl sulfonamide with para-aldehyde.

3. Disconnection of sulfonamide formation: from sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride?) and aniline (the first phenyl ring). Actually the sulfonamide is between the first phenyl (with methyl) and the second phenyl (the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl). Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the nitrogen attached to first phenyl (methyl phenyl) is the sulfonamide nitrogen. So the sulfonyl chloride would be p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl) reacting with aniline (the second phenyl? Actually the nitrogen is attached to first phenyl, not second. The nitrogen is attached to first phenyl (the methyl phenyl) and to sulfonyl group. So the sulfonyl chloride is attached to second phenyl (c2...). So the sulfonyl chloride is 4-(... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride would be the sulfonyl group attached to the second phenyl ring (the one bearing the side chain). So we need sulfonyl chloride derived from that phenyl ring (with aldehyde). So we can make sulfonyl chloride from that phenyl (by chlorosulfonation). Then react with the first phenyl amine (p-toluidine). So third step: sulfonyl chloride formation from aromatic ring (with aldehyde) and then sulfonamide formation.

Thus three steps: (1) amide coupling, (2) Doebner condensation to form α,β-unsaturated acid, (3) sulfonyl chloride formation and sulfonamide coupling.
